elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: TrueLink must “defend” Client and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Interface, Hosting Services, or Support Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The same provision expressly requires TrueLink to “indemnify” Client and its affiliates for those IP claims.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The defense obligation applies to any third-party claim arising from “TrueLink's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation applies to any third-party claim arising from “TrueLink's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The defense covers third-party claims arising from unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data “caused by TrueLink.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnification covers third-party claims arising from unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data “caused by TrueLink.”

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The defense obligation expressly covers claims arising from “TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation expressly covers claims arising from “TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.”

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor with prompt notice of a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Client “shall promptly notify TrueLink of any such claim.”

elements.element: Vendor must control the defense and settlement of a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim.”

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Client to “provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must include claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Client indemnifies TrueLink for claims “arising out of or relating to Client Content,” the operative customer-content category.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must include claims arising from Customer's own breach of law.
elements.evidence: Client indemnifies TrueLink for “any violation of any state or federal law, rule or regulation by Client.”

elements.element: Customer must have no indemnity triggers beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's own breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered Client indemnity contains only two enumerated triggers: Client Content and violations of law by Client; the original broader breach, downstream-customer, website, product, and personal/property injury triggers were removed.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: TrueLink expressly indemnifies Client against third-party claims alleging infringement or misappropriation by the Interface, Hosting Services, or Support Services.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion for modifications made by Client.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no combination exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion for Client-provided designs, instructions, or specifications.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No procurement or continued-use remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing alternatives.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund remedy for affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a distinct elevated super-cap.
elements.evidence: No indemnification super-cap or other liability cap is stated in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnification super-cap must equal three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no 3× annual-fees limitation.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: it adds defense and indemnity for all four required Vendor-risk categories, protects Client and its affiliates, includes notice/control/cooperation procedures, and confines Client's indemnity triggers to Client Content and Client violations of law. It does not satisfy the fallback because all specified IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The changes are substantively targeted and preserve unrelated terms, but drafting quality is reduced by the duplicative Vendor-indemnity provisions and the awkward legacy wording “hold Client harmless, its affiliates ... harmless.”
